name: claude-skills
description: Ioannis Antoniadis' personal collection of Claude Code skills and plugins.

plugins.name: interview-prep-repo
plugins.description: Scaffold a tailored, research-backed interview-prep repo for an upcoming job interview — topic pages, a cram brief, rehearsable prompts, glossary, notes distilled from real papers/blog posts, and (for hands-on rounds) a small runnable code scaffold with passing tests.

plugins.name: algorithm-visualizer
plugins.description: Add a new algorithm to an existing Streamlit + Plotly algorithm-visualizer portfolio repo — from-scratch NumPy implementation, step-by-step Plotly visualization, matching the repo's established theme, session-state, and playback conventions.

plugins.name: ai-topic-note
plugins.description: Add a new topic, or extend an existing one, to an existing personal AI/ML knowledge-base repo in its established terse-reference-prose style, deciding granularity (new file vs. subsection) and updating only the index files that actually apply.

plugins.name: white-paper
plugins.description: Turn a rough idea into a researched, well-argued white paper: the author's input kept verbatim, research including the evidence against, a structured template (thesis, assumptions, scenarios, path, counterarguments), then review and revision.

plugins.name: skeptical-review
plugins.description: Critique papers, proposals and plans like a hard but fair referee: verified citations, counter-evidence and prior art, anchored 1–5 rubrics, hard fails, ranked issues with fixes, and decisions for the author.

plugins.name: learning-repo
plugins.description: Build, audit and compare learning repos (technical books, notes, algorithm demos): one shared rubric for building and auditing (primary-source research, figures from real computation, claims that match measurements, tests that check the claims, internal consistency, clean builds), and a blinded comparison that counts confirmed defects per 10,000 words.
